courses.course_name: Introduction to Windows PC Systems Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to administer a Windows personal computer (PC) that will be connected to an industrial network. The concepts developed in this course prepares students for the Linux Systems Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term two. Topics include: an introduction to PC hardware, functions of an operating system (OS), Windows OS architecture, file and disk management, BIOS and UEFI, multi-boot, virtual machines, software installation/removal, performance tuning, backing up and protecting data, troubleshooting, networking, security, virus protection, firewalls, and Windows PC hardening for connection to an industrial network. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Python Scripting for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to articulate the solution to a technical problem within the bounds of the Python programming language. The concepts developed in this course prepares students for the Linux Systems Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term two. Students will learn how to design, implement, test, and debug programs that incorporate: variables, expressions, assignments, I/O, conditional and iterative control constructs, functions, and parameter passing. Programming related activities, assignments, and projects that are representative of tasks encounter in the IT workplace are used to facilitate the development of programming skills. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Technical Communications 1 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to the basics of technical writing and develops the skills needed to write effective technical documents. The competencies developed in this course will be used throughout the INC program. Many courses from the second term forward will include some form of technical writing which will be included in the courses’ evaluations. Topics include: writing common technical documents such as progress, trip, field, laboratory, and design reports; writing effective letters and emails; writing technical descriptions and instructions; creating appropriate tables, charts, graphs and illustrations; and using proper citation. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Electrical Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: MATH 1600 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides a foundation in simple circuits comprised of basic passive and active electrical components. The concepts developed in this course prepares students for the Industrial Systems and Safety for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Programmable Logic Controllers course in term two. Topics include: Ohm’s Law, basic circuit analysis, passive components (resistors, capacitors, and inductors), active components (diodes, transistors, etc.), electrical devices (switches, sensors, etc.), and wiring diagrams. Simple circuits using active and passive components will be built and tested using a multimeter. Corequisite: MATH 1431*, Technical Mathematics for Electronics (* (*may be taken concurrently) Prerequisite(s): MATH 1600 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Networking Fundamentals
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides a foundation in computer networking with an emphasis on how networks exchange information via routers and switches. The concepts developed in this course prepares students for the Advanced Networking course in term two. Topics include Ethernet technologies, the TCP/IP protocol stack, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, VLANs and VLAN trunking, static and dynamic routing, access control lists, and network address translation. Students will learn to connect to Cisco devices and using a command-line interface be able to configure basic settings in the lab. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Technical Mathematics for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides a foundation in basic algebra, transcendental functions, and Boolean algebra. The concepts developed in this course prepares students for the Calculus course in term two. The concepts taught in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Electrical Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity , Python Scripting for Industrial Network Cybersecurity , Introduction to Systems Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity , and Networking Fundamentals courses. Topics include: numbering systems; the conversion between numbering systems; Boolean algebra and techniques; Boolean expressions; approximate numbers; exponents and radicals; exponentials and logarithms; complex numbers; and solving systems of linear equations. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Linux System Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 1421
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to administrate a Linux System that is connected to an industrial network. Building on the concepts developed in the Python Scripting for Industrial Network Cybersecurity , and Introduction to Windows PC Systems Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term one, this course prepares students for the Industrial Networking course in the following five week term, and the Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity , and Embedded Systems courses in term three. Topics include installing and configuring software; adding hardware; networking servers; configuring common server services such as DNS, DHCP, Apache and IP Tables; managing users; monitoring performance; scripting; troubleshooting; and Linux system hardening for connection to an industrial network. Prerequisite(s): ACIT 1421

courses.course_name: Industrial Systems and Safety for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: COMM 1130 and ELEX 1610 MATH 2061 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces common industrial processes and systems that will be encounter by an INC graduate. Building on the concepts learned in the Electrical Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term one, this course prepares students for the Industrial Networking course in the following five week term and the Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three. The concepts taught in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Programmable Logic Controllers and Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses. Topics include: pumps, heat exchangers, material handling systems, food and chemical processes, evaporator/distillation processes, boiler systems, turbines, evaporators, distillation columns, pulp digester and pulp stock blending, hydro and thermal power generation systems, and workplace safety practices. This course includes one or more field trips to local industrial facilities which will require protective clothing. Prerequisite(s): COMM 1130 and ELEX 1610 MATH 2061 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: COMM 1130 and ELEX 1610 MATH 2061 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces fundamental engineering principles that underpin the physical phenomena encountered by an INC graduate. Building on the concepts developed in the Electrical Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term one, this course prepares students for the Industrial Networking course in the following five-week term and the Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three. The concepts taught in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Programmable Logic Controllers and Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses. Topics include: kinematics and dynamics of translational and rotational motion, conservation of energy, simple harmonic motion, electrical and magnetic fields, wave propagation, magnetic circuits, basic thermodynamics (Law of Conservation of Energy) and heat transfer, and basic fluid mechanics (Bernoulli’s equation). ​ Prerequisite(s): COMM 1130 and ELEX 1610 MATH 2061 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Advanced Networking
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 1110
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops the skills necessary to plan, install, configure and troubleshoot devices and protocols used to implement a scalable campus LAN. Building on the concepts developed in the Networking Fundamentals course in term one, this course prepares students for the Industrial Networking course in the following five-week term. Topics include: deployment of wireless services using Wireless LAN controllers, Spanning-tree Protocol (STP), First-Hop Redundancy for hosts on subnets, port aggregation, link-state routing protocol versus distance vector routing protocol operations, device discovery tools, logging services, and switch port security. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 1110

courses.course_name: Programmable Logic Controllers
courses.prerequisite_raw: ELEX 2610 † and ELEX 2620 † ( † may be taken concurrently) ELEX 2610 ‡ and ELEX 2620 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops a working knowledge of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) to provide a deep appreciation as to their application in industry and the challenges associated with the networking and network security of them. Building on the concepts learned in the Electrical Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity and Technical Mathematics for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term one, this course prepares students for the Industrial Networking course in the following five-week term. Topics include: an overview of PLCs, their industrial applications, and a survey of the programming languages conforming to the IEC-61131-3 standard. A step-by-step approach is used to interface devices to a PLC. Lab activities include the creation of a simple sequential and ON/OFF control system and the implementation of Ethernet communications to integrate an HMI touchscreen display. ​ Prerequisite(s): ELEX 2610 † and ELEX 2620 † ( † may be taken concurrently) ELEX 2610 ‡ and ELEX 2620 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: 50% in MATH 1600
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides the foundation in the calculus needed to solve problems involving integration and differentiation. Building on the concepts developed in the Technical Mathematics for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term one, this course prepares students for the Process Measurement and Control Fundaments for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Industrial Systems and Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses. Topics include: the differentiation and integration of common algebraic and transcendental functions; first and second order differential equations; negative feedback; and the proportional, integral and derivative (PID) control algorithm. ​ Prerequisite(s): 50% in MATH 1600

courses.course_name: Industrial Networking
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2110 and ACIT 2421 and ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and INCS 2610 and MATH 2601
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops the skills needed to support an industrial network based on the Purdue five-layer model. Building on the concepts developed in the Advanced Networking in term two, this course prepares students to work on industrial networks. Topics include: the difference between business and industrial networks with an emphasis on the importance of business continuity and the need for real time performance and determinism in industrial systems; a history of IT/OT convergence; Wide Area Networks; Industrial Ethernet; serial interfaces; industrial protocols; and channel media. Prerequisite(s): INCS 2110 and ACIT 2421 and ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and INCS 2610 and MATH 2601

courses.course_name: Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to administrate a Microsoft Windows Server that is connected to an industrial network. Building on the concepts learned in the Linux System Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term two, this course prepares students for the Introduction to Virtualization and Databases for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Industrial Network Security course. Topics include: local and remote server management; server storage; Active Directory (AD); managing organization units and AD accounts; configuring group policies; TCP/IP in Windows network; Domain Name System (DNS); and Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). Students configure a Windows Server to perform a variety of roles, including acting as a DNS server, DHCP server, and file server. During the course students will build a Windows domain consisting of three or more Windows and Linux virtual machines, and learn to troubleshoot and monitor a Windows domain environment.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and MATH 2601
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides a basic working knowledge of process measurement and control systems to provide a deep appreciation as to their application in industry and the challenges associated with the networking and network security of them. Building on the concepts developed in the Industrial Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term three, this course prepares students for the Distributed Control and Safety Instrumented Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Embedded Systems and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: transducers and instruments used for measuring pressure, level, flow, and temperature; open- and closed-loop control; ON/OFF and Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) control; and advanced control strategies including feedforward and cascade. Lab activities will include commissioning a simple control loop. ​ Prerequisite(s): ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and MATH 2601

courses.course_name: Industrial Network Security
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2210 ACIT 3421 ‡ and ELEX 3610 ‡ and INCS 3320 ‡ and INCS 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the security principles and technologies used to secure an industrial network. Building on the concepts developed in the Industrial Networking course in term two, this course prepares students for the Cyber Operations course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Embedded Systems courses. Topics include: vulnerabilities with operating systems; methods of attacks; defense-in-depth strategies; security appliances including firewalls, IDS and IPS; IPSec and VPNs; Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA); security monitoring; evasion methods; and interpreting log data to identify events in Windows and Linux systems. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 2210 ACIT 3421 ‡ and ELEX 3610 ‡ and INCS 3320 ‡ and INCS 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2210 INCS 3310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to perform all phases of a penetration test on an industrial network using Kali Linux as a penetration testing platform. Building on the concepts developed in the second term Industrial Networking course, this course prepares students to use penetration testing to validate the configuration of security appliances and gather information as part of a risk analysis. The concepts being developed in this course relate closely with the concepts being developed in the concurrent third term Linux Administration and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: performing reconnaissance, scanning an industrial network, identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities, and maintaining post exploitation. Tools and techniques that may be used include: Google Directives, theHarvester, Whois, Host, HTTrack, Netcraft, Metagoofil, ThreatAgent, Ping, Nmap, Nessus, Wireshark, John the Ripper, Metasploit, Armitage, Medusa, Password Resetting, Netcat, Cryptcat, Metasploit Meterpreter, and the Hacker Defender rootkit. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 2210 INCS 3310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Embedded Systems
courses.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 2421 and INCS 2610 ELEX 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to the role of embedded systems found within most modern control devices to develop an appreciation for their vulnerability to cyber-attacks . Building on the concepts developed in the Programmable Logic Controller and Linux Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term two, this course prepares students for the Cyber Operations course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: the operation of a microprocessor, the difference between microcontrollers and microprocessors, the role of machine code, the difference between assembly language and machine code, and the role of higher-level programs and how they are distinguished from assembly language programs. Using a Raspberry Pi students will create a system that acquires a measurement from the external environment and uses that measurement to change the environment by means of a final control element and then demonstrate the exploitation of a known vulnerability of the Linux OS to affect the system’s performance. ​ Prerequisite(s): ACIT 2421 and INCS 2610 ELEX 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Virtualization and Database Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 3421
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops a working knowledge of virtualization and database systems to provide a deep understanding that industrial networks often extend into a virtualized server or workstation running a relational database. Building on the concepts developed in the Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three, this course prepares students for the Culmination Project in the following five-week term. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Cyber Operations course. Topics include: the implementation and configuration of Microsoft’s Hyper-V, the installation of a relational database on a virtual machine, creating a database and database objects, querying a database using SQL, security issues with relational databases, and data protection techniques for relational databases. Prerequisite(s): ACIT 3421

courses.course_name: Technical Communication 2 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: COMM 1130
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops the skills necessary to be an efficient and professional communicator in the INC field. Building on the skills learned in the Technical Communication 1 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in the first term, this course prepares students for the formal report and oral presentation portion of the Culminating Project. Topics include how to: conduct an effective job search and write the accompanying resume, LinkedIn profile, and cover letter; develop strategies for persuasion and for delivering negative messages; and write an effective proposal, identify the parts of a formal report, and deliver an oral presentation. Students will practice teamwork skills and participate effectively in meetings and group work. ​ Prerequisite(s): COMM 1130

courses.course_name: Distributed Control and Safety Instrumented Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: ELEX 3610
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course develops a basic working knowledge of distributed control and safety instrumented systems to provide a deep appreciation as to their application in industry and the challenges associated with the networking and network security of them. Building on the concepts developed in the Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three, this course prepares students for the Culminating Project in the five-week term that follows. Topics include: programming languages conforming to the IEC-61131-3 (FBDs, SFCs and structured text), the theory of advanced control strategies including multivariable and statistical process controls (SPC), trips, interlocks, permissives, and sequence control. Laboratory activities involve the configuration and operation of a distributed control system platform (DeltaV), to implement and test control strategies on typical industrial processes. Prerequisite(s): ELEX 3610

courses.course_name: Cyber Operations
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 and INCS 3610 INCS 4320 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides a foundation in cyber operations as it relates to industrial networks. Building on the concepts learned in the Industrial Network Security, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, and Embedded Systems courses in term three, this course prepares students for the Culminating Project in the following five-week term. The concepts taught in this course relate closely with the concepts being taught concurrently in the Databases and Virtualization for Industrial Network Cybersecurity and ICS Cybersecurity Standards courses. Topics include performing a risk and network intrusion analysis, creating an incident response plan, assisting with a computer forensics instigation, and the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 and INCS 3610 INCS 4320 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: ICS Cybersecurity Standards
courses.prerequisite_raw: INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 INCS 4310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces common Industrial Control System (ICS) cybersecurity standards that INC graduates will encounter in the workplace. Building on the concepts developed in the Linux Administration, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, and Industrial Network Security courses, this course prepares students to assist with implementing common ICS cyber security standards as they apply to industrial networks. Topics include: the differences between policies, standards, procedures, guidelines and frameworks ; a general overview of the steps involved in an ICS security standard; the difference between enterprise/business IT security standards and ICS security standards; a survey of ICS cybersecurity standards commonly used in both North America and Europe and their application in automation and process control; and a close look at all three phases of the ISA/IEC 62443 standard with an emphasis on risk assessment and mitigation. ICS standards and frameworks studied include ISA/IEC 62443, NIST 800-82 and NERC CIP. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 INCS 4310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.course_name: Technical Communication 3 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisite_raw: COMM 2130
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides support for preparing a formal report and delivering an oral presentation for the Culminating Project. Building on the skills developed in COMM 2130 Technical Communication 2 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, students will: prepare a formal report and deliver an oral presentation for the Culminating Project; practice teamwork skills; and participate effectively in meetings and group work. ​ Prerequisite(s): COMM 2130

courses.course_name: Culminating Project
courses.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 4421 and ELEX 4610 and INCS 4310 and INCS 4320 COMM 2230 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: This project cements the knowledge learnt in the program by taking the steps necessary to analyze an industrial network, identify vulnerabilities, perform a risk analysis, recommend actions that can be taken to reduce the risk, and create an incident response plan in accordance with the ISA-62443 standard. Students work in teams and seek advice from a faculty member acting as their project supervisor. At the end of the project students submit an individually prepared formal report and participant in a group presentation. ​ Prerequisite(s): ACIT 4421 and ELEX 4610 and INCS 4310 and INCS 4320 COMM 2230 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

Topics include: an overview of PLCs, their industrial applications, and a survey of the programming languages conforming to the IEC-61131-3 standard. A step-by-step approach is used to interface devices to a PLC. Lab activities include the creation of a simple sequential and ON/OFF control system and the implementation of Ethernet communications to integrate an HMI touchscreen display. ​ Prerequisite(s): ELEX 2610 † and ELEX 2620 † ( † may be taken concurrently) ELEX 2610 ‡ and ELEX 2620 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: 50% in MATH 1600
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course provides the foundation in the calculus needed to solve problems involving integration and differentiation. Building on the concepts developed in the Technical Mathematics for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term one, this course prepares students for the Process Measurement and Control Fundaments for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Industrial Systems and Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses. Topics include: the differentiation and integration of common algebraic and transcendental functions; first and second order differential equations; negative feedback; and the proportional, integral and derivative (PID) control algorithm. ​ Prerequisite(s): 50% in MATH 1600

course_references.course_name: Industrial Networking
course_references.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2110 and ACIT 2421 and ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and INCS 2610 and MATH 2601
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course develops the skills needed to support an industrial network based on the Purdue five-layer model. Building on the concepts developed in the Advanced Networking in term two, this course prepares students to work on industrial networks. Topics include: the difference between business and industrial networks with an emphasis on the importance of business continuity and the need for real time performance and determinism in industrial systems; a history of IT/OT convergence; Wide Area Networks; Industrial Ethernet; serial interfaces; industrial protocols; and channel media. Prerequisite(s): INCS 2110 and ACIT 2421 and ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and INCS 2610 and MATH 2601

course_references.course_name: Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to administrate a Microsoft Windows Server that is connected to an industrial network. Building on the concepts learned in the Linux System Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term two, this course prepares students for the Introduction to Virtualization and Databases for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Industrial Network Security course. Topics include: local and remote server management; server storage; Active Directory (AD); managing organization units and AD accounts; configuring group policies; TCP/IP in Windows network; Domain Name System (DNS); and Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). Students configure a Windows Server to perform a variety of roles, including acting as a DNS server, DHCP server, and file server. During the course students will build a Windows domain consisting of three or more Windows and Linux virtual machines, and learn to troubleshoot and monitor a Windows domain environment.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

course_references.course_name: Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and MATH 2601
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course provides a basic working knowledge of process measurement and control systems to provide a deep appreciation as to their application in industry and the challenges associated with the networking and network security of them. Building on the concepts developed in the Industrial Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, Calculus for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Engineering Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term three, this course prepares students for the Distributed Control and Safety Instrumented Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Embedded Systems and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: transducers and instruments used for measuring pressure, level, flow, and temperature; open- and closed-loop control; ON/OFF and Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) control; and advanced control strategies including feedforward and cascade. Lab activities will include commissioning a simple control loop. ​ Prerequisite(s): ELEX 2610 and ELEX 2620 and MATH 2601

course_references.course_name: Industrial Network Security
course_references.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2210 ACIT 3421 ‡ and ELEX 3610 ‡ and INCS 3320 ‡ and INCS 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the security principles and technologies used to secure an industrial network. Building on the concepts developed in the Industrial Networking course in term two, this course prepares students for the Cyber Operations course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Embedded Systems courses. Topics include: vulnerabilities with operating systems; methods of attacks; defense-in-depth strategies; security appliances including firewalls, IDS and IPS; IPSec and VPNs; Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA); security monitoring; evasion methods; and interpreting log data to identify events in Windows and Linux systems. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 2210 ACIT 3421 ‡ and ELEX 3610 ‡ and INCS 3320 ‡ and INCS 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing
course_references.prerequisite_raw: INCS 2210 INCS 3310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course introduces the skills necessary to perform all phases of a penetration test on an industrial network using Kali Linux as a penetration testing platform. Building on the concepts developed in the second term Industrial Networking course, this course prepares students to use penetration testing to validate the configuration of security appliances and gather information as part of a risk analysis. The concepts being developed in this course relate closely with the concepts being developed in the concurrent third term Linux Administration and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: performing reconnaissance, scanning an industrial network, identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities, and maintaining post exploitation. Tools and techniques that may be used include: Google Directives, theHarvester, Whois, Host, HTTrack, Netcraft, Metagoofil, ThreatAgent, Ping, Nmap, Nessus, Wireshark, John the Ripper, Metasploit, Armitage, Medusa, Password Resetting, Netcat, Cryptcat, Metasploit Meterpreter, and the Hacker Defender rootkit. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 2210 INCS 3310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: Embedded Systems
course_references.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 2421 and INCS 2610 ELEX 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to the role of embedded systems found within most modern control devices to develop an appreciation for their vulnerability to cyber-attacks . Building on the concepts developed in the Programmable Logic Controller and Linux Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity courses in term two, this course prepares students for the Cyber Operations course in term four. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, and Industrial Network Security courses. Topics include: the operation of a microprocessor, the difference between microcontrollers and microprocessors, the role of machine code, the difference between assembly language and machine code, and the role of higher-level programs and how they are distinguished from assembly language programs. Using a Raspberry Pi students will create a system that acquires a measurement from the external environment and uses that measurement to change the environment by means of a final control element and then demonstrate the exploitation of a known vulnerability of the Linux OS to affect the system’s performance. ​ Prerequisite(s): ACIT 2421 and INCS 2610 ELEX 3610 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: Virtualization and Database Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 3421
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course develops a working knowledge of virtualization and database systems to provide a deep understanding that industrial networks often extend into a virtualized server or workstation running a relational database. Building on the concepts developed in the Windows Server Administration for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three, this course prepares students for the Culmination Project in the following five-week term. The concepts being developed in this course are closely related to the concepts being developed concurrently in the Cyber Operations course. Topics include: the implementation and configuration of Microsoft’s Hyper-V, the installation of a relational database on a virtual machine, creating a database and database objects, querying a database using SQL, security issues with relational databases, and data protection techniques for relational databases. Prerequisite(s): ACIT 3421

course_references.course_name: Technical Communication 2 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: COMM 1130
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course develops the skills necessary to be an efficient and professional communicator in the INC field. Building on the skills learned in the Technical Communication 1 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in the first term, this course prepares students for the formal report and oral presentation portion of the Culminating Project. Topics include how to: conduct an effective job search and write the accompanying resume, LinkedIn profile, and cover letter; develop strategies for persuasion and for delivering negative messages; and write an effective proposal, identify the parts of a formal report, and deliver an oral presentation. Students will practice teamwork skills and participate effectively in meetings and group work. ​ Prerequisite(s): COMM 1130

course_references.course_name: Distributed Control and Safety Instrumented Systems for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: ELEX 3610
course_references.course_overview_raw: ​This course develops a basic working knowledge of distributed control and safety instrumented systems to provide a deep appreciation as to their application in industry and the challenges associated with the networking and network security of them. Building on the concepts developed in the Process Measurement and Control Fundamentals for Industrial Network Cybersecurity course in term three, this course prepares students for the Culminating Project in the five-week term that follows. Topics include: programming languages conforming to the IEC-61131-3 (FBDs, SFCs and structured text), the theory of advanced control strategies including multivariable and statistical process controls (SPC), trips, interlocks, permissives, and sequence control. Laboratory activities involve the configuration and operation of a distributed control system platform (DeltaV), to implement and test control strategies on typical industrial processes. Prerequisite(s): ELEX 3610

course_references.course_name: Cyber Operations
course_references.prerequisite_raw: INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 and INCS 3610 INCS 4320 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course provides a foundation in cyber operations as it relates to industrial networks. Building on the concepts learned in the Industrial Network Security, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, and Embedded Systems courses in term three, this course prepares students for the Culminating Project in the following five-week term. The concepts taught in this course relate closely with the concepts being taught concurrently in the Databases and Virtualization for Industrial Network Cybersecurity and ICS Cybersecurity Standards courses. Topics include performing a risk and network intrusion analysis, creating an incident response plan, assisting with a computer forensics instigation, and the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 and INCS 3610 INCS 4320 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: ICS Cybersecurity Standards
course_references.prerequisite_raw: INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 INCS 4310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course introduces common Industrial Control System (ICS) cybersecurity standards that INC graduates will encounter in the workplace. Building on the concepts developed in the Linux Administration, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, and Industrial Network Security courses, this course prepares students to assist with implementing common ICS cyber security standards as they apply to industrial networks. Topics include: the differences between policies, standards, procedures, guidelines and frameworks ; a general overview of the steps involved in an ICS security standard; the difference between enterprise/business IT security standards and ICS security standards; a survey of ICS cybersecurity standards commonly used in both North America and Europe and their application in automation and process control; and a close look at all three phases of the ISA/IEC 62443 standard with an emphasis on risk assessment and mitigation. ICS standards and frameworks studied include ISA/IEC 62443, NIST 800-82 and NERC CIP. ​ Prerequisite(s): INCS 3310 and INCS 3320 INCS 4310 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

course_references.course_name: Technical Communication 3 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity
course_references.prerequisite_raw: COMM 2130
course_references.course_overview_raw: This course provides support for preparing a formal report and delivering an oral presentation for the Culminating Project. Building on the skills developed in COMM 2130 Technical Communication 2 for Industrial Network Cybersecurity, students will: prepare a formal report and deliver an oral presentation for the Culminating Project; practice teamwork skills; and participate effectively in meetings and group work. ​ Prerequisite(s): COMM 2130

course_references.course_name: Culminating Project
course_references.prerequisite_raw: ACIT 4421 and ELEX 4610 and INCS 4310 and INCS 4320 COMM 2230 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
course_references.course_overview_raw: This project cements the knowledge learnt in the program by taking the steps necessary to analyze an industrial network, identify vulnerabilities, perform a risk analysis, recommend actions that can be taken to reduce the risk, and create an incident response plan in accordance with the ISA-62443 standard. Students work in teams and seek advice from a faculty member acting as their project supervisor. At the end of the project students submit an individually prepared formal report and participant in a group presentation. ​ Prerequisite(s): ACIT 4421 and ELEX 4610 and INCS 4310 and INCS 4320 COMM 2230 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted during the following periods: Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intake may fill before the deadline. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis, as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 12 (67%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses Chemistry 11 (67%) Physics 11 (67%) Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Note : Applicants who are currently enrolled in the Technology Entry (TE) program may receive conditional acceptance, subject to successfully completing the program and any applicable entrance requirement courses. Recommended for success Strong mathematic skills are required for success in this program. If you would like to upgrade your mathematic skills, or any of the entrance requirements listed above, you should consider taking the Technology Entry (TE) program . International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. ( CIPC : 11.1003) Transfer credit Do you have credits from another post-secondary school? Transfer credit may be granted for courses completed at another post-secondary institution where the learning outcomes duplicate those of the BCIT course. The Industrial Network Cybersecurity program reserves the right to determine the granting of credit where appropriate. Please contact us for details. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for re-admission may still be submitted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) Prior Learning Assessment Recognition (PLAR) lets you use knowledge and skills learned outside recognized programs to gain exemption for particular courses in the Industrial Network Cybersecurity program. Please contact us for details. Technology entry The Technology Entry (TE) program is a full-time, day school program which provides academic upgrading to students wishing to enroll in Computing, Engineering, Electronic, and Health Sciences programs at BCIT. The TE program provides courses in chemistry, communication, mathematics, and physics that meet program prerequisites for selected programs at BCIT. The TE program also includes an introductory course in computer applications and a learning skills course. The program is supportive to those who require English-language training. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
